title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Pliny rue and weasel: the depicted animal consumes protection before danger
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Pliny reports weasels consuming rue before attacking serpents. Bind an animal as the actor and beneficiary of plant consumption, then a distinct dangerous opponent and later encounter. This is prospective self-protection, not a picture naming the disease which a human remedy treats.

source.span: Volume IV, chapter 51, Rue: eighty-four remedies
source.observed_content: Pliny reports weasels consuming rue before attacking serpents.

design.mechanism: Bind an animal as the actor and beneficiary of plant consumption, then a distinct dangerous opponent and later encounter. This is prospective self-protection, not a picture naming the disease which a human remedy treats.
design.unit: Whole plant-animal entry and both action/encounter clauses; preserve who eats, who attacks whom, and the temporal direction.
design.contrast: A bite-treatment account has injury before remedy; a deterrent account has the animal avoid contact. The source account instead has consumption before an animal-initiated encounter.
design.prediction: A future complete target reading must preserve the same animal across consumption and encounter while assigning the serpent a different role. Animal adjacency or a guessed BEFORE word alone cannot do this.
